la:other:Maia.gloss: Daughter of Atlas and mother of Hermes.
senses: Daughter of Atlas and mother of Hermes.
The goddess of growth after whom the month May (Latin maius) was named.
A star in the constellation Taurus. It is the fourth brightest star in the Pleiades cluster.

la:noun:maiestas.html:
mājestas, ātis, f.
major, magnus, q. v.
,
greatness, grandeur, dignity, majesty.
Lit., of the gods; also the condition of men in high station, as kings, consuls, senators, knights, etc., and, in republican states, esp. freq. of the people (class.).
Of the gods: di non censent esse suae majestatis, praesignificare hominibus, quae sunt futura,: primus est deorum cultus deos credere, deinde reddere illis majestatem suam,: divinam majestatem asserere sibi coepit,divine majesty,.—
Of men: consulis,: judicum,: regia,: ducis,: senatus,: patria,the paternal authority,: inter nos sanctissima divitiarum majestas,.—The sovereign power, sovereignty of the Roman people: majestatem populi Romani defendere,: per majestatem populi Romani subvenite misero mihi,: ad tantam magnitudinem Romana majestas cunctorum numinum favore pervenit, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 6, 4, 6: majestatem minuere or laedere, to injure or offend against the majesty, sovereignty of the people: majestatem minuere est de dignitate, aut amplitudine, aut potestate populi, aut eorum, quibus populus potestatem dedit, aliquid derogare,; : populi Romani majestatem laedere,; ; ; : crimen majestatis, high-treason; an offence against the majesty, sovereignty of the people: et crimen majestatis, quod imperii nostri gloriae, rerumque gestarum monumenta evertere atque asportare ausus est,: legionem sollicitare, res est, quae lege majestatis tenetur,against treason,: condemnatus majestatis,: laesae majestatis accusari,: majestatis causā damnatus,: majestatis judicium,: Lege Julia majestatis tenetur is, cujus ope, consilio adversus imperatorem vel rem publicam arma mota sunt, exercitusve ejus in insidias deductus est,.—As a title of honor of the Roman emperors, majesty, ; et saep.—
Transf., in gen., honor, dignity, excellence,
